newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound two Arabs in Gaza clash.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound two Arabs in Gaza clash.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded two Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday in clashes with hundreds of Arabs who planted olive trees on land seized by Jewish settlers, hospital officials and witnesses said.

They said other Palestinians were overcome by tear gas. The clash erupted after Arab demonstrators knocked down a fence put up around hothouses by residents of the Jewish settlement of Morag. Protesters say the fence intrudes on Palestinian-owned property.
An Israeli army spokesman said he was aware of "some kind of gathering" in Khan Younis, and was checking the report. Israeli soldiers guarding the Morag enclave have deployed tanks in the area.
The director of Khan Younis hospital in Gaza said a middle-aged Palestinian was shot in the chest and a bullet grazed the head of another Arab. Neither was in critical condition.
Witnesses said at least four others were overcome by tear gas and had to be evacuated from the site.
"They fired live ammunition in the air and tear gas and rubber bullets at the crowd," a witness told Reuters.

Another witness said Palestinian police struggled to separate demonstrators and Israeli soldiers who deployed in large numbers near the site and tried to pluck out Palestinian flags raised by protesters on the land.
Palestinians have been camping on the land since June 2 when Jewish settlers fenced it off, provoking scuffles with Israeli soldiers in which five Arabs were hurt.

An Israeli spokesman said at the time the fence was intended to protect flower plantations from thieves. He said contacts were underway with the Palestinian side to determine if the fence intruded on private property.
Palestinian-Israeli tension has been running high since the Jewish state began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, prompting clashes in parts of the West Bank.
Sixty one Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in clashes which erupted last year after Israel opened a second entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem's Old City.
